title: Mission 16: The Runaway
story: Alerts at 3 AM: something called runaway_miner is eating the box, a stuck monitor refuses every polite request to stop, and the logging service needs a nudge - not a bullet. Processes are living things: ps sees them, kill talks to them. Most of what kill says is not 'die' - and knowing the difference is the whole job.

badge.name: The Runaway: Contained
badge.desc: Mastered ps and kill by finding rogue processes, escalating signals correctly and sparing the innocent.

tasks.brief: Read BRIEFING16.txt in your department directory. The legitimate report_daemon is running. Find its PID (ps aux piped through the search you know, or pgrep) and write JUST the number to ops/daemon_pid.txt.

checks.fail: daemon_pid.txt must contain report_daemon's live PID (pgrep -f finds by name; the daemon must still be running).

tasks.brief: Prove the reverse lookup too: using ps with that PID, write the process's COMMAND NAME (just the name, exactly as ps -o comm= prints it - the kernel clips names to 15 characters, and that clipped form is the answer) to ops/daemon_name.txt.

checks.fail: daemon_name.txt must contain exactly what ps -o comm= -p <pid> prints for the daemon (note: the kernel truncates command names to 15 characters - what you see is what you save).

tasks.brief: The runaway_miner dies politely: send it the DEFAULT termination signal (plain kill, or pkill by name). It must be gone.

checks.fail: runaway_miner is still running (find its PID, send the default TERM signal).

tasks.brief: gridmon_stuck IGNORES polite requests (it traps TERM - try it and watch it survive). Some processes only stop for the one signal nothing can trap. Escalate and take it down.

checks.fail: gridmon_stuck is still running. It traps TERM; only signal 9 (KILL) cannot be trapped.

tasks.brief: logger_svc reloads its config when it receives USR1 - no restart needed. Send it USR1 (kill -USR1 <pid>). When it worked, the service drops a reload receipt at ops/logger_reloaded (watch for it).

checks.fail: No reload receipt yet - logger_svc has not received USR1 (signals are messages; USR1 here means 'reload', not 'die').
logger_svc is DEAD. USR1 reloads; you sent something fatal. (Relaunch the mission to restore it.)
report_daemon was killed. Contain the rogues; never shotgun every process that looks unusual.

tasks.brief: BONUS: the hexlab_worker pool - how many worker processes are running right now? pgrep can count for you. Just the number to ops/workercount.txt.

checks.fail: workercount.txt must match the live hexlab_worker count (pgrep has a count option; the workers are still running, right?).
